title: Marketplace onboarding runbook: SKU mapping + security checklist
body:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook is a single-source working doc for preparing Redwood Inference listings on cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP) focused on enterprise SKUs, security preflight, copy variants, and billing mapping. It is intended for go-to-market, legal, product, and engineering partners who are shepherding a listing from internal signoff to marketplace publication.

High-level goals:
- Produce SKU and pricing mapping that aligns with internal dedicated/private product packaging and marketplace SKU constraints.
- Create concise marketing copy variants for each marketplace channel (short, mid, long) plus a 1-line elevator pitch for vendor pages.
- Verify security/compliance checklist items required by marketplaces (data residency, SOC/ISO statements, KMS integration notes).
- Define technical artifact list and test-plan for listing QA.

Quick notes / context:
- Audience: Procurement and platform teams at buyers; technical buyers expect clear callouts for VPC/private deployment pricing and SLAs.
- Constraint: Some marketplaces force a single SKU per region; plan bundling strategy for Dedicated vs Private.
- Known blockers: legal needs final indemnity language (see linked JIRA MKTP-4123).

1) SKU mapping and price bundles (working table)
- SKU: Redwood-Hosted-Standard -> Marketplace SKU ID TBD -> Unit: Monthly -> Notes: public API, pay-as-you-go pricing model, map to hosted-tier pricing in pricebook.
- SKU: Redwood-Dedicated-4x -> Marketplace SKU: reserved-dedicated-4 -> Unit: Monthly commitment -> Notes: equivalent to internal Dedicated-4; set minimum commit of $5k/mo to match infra floor.
- SKU: Redwood-Private-VPC -> Marketplace SKU: private-deployment -> Unit: Annual license + managed support -> Notes: marketplace listing should offer "Contact us" flow (no direct procurement unless enterprise contract).
- Decision needed: Should Dedicated burst capacity be an add-on SKU or included in Dedicated-4? (ACTION: pricing lead to advise by 2025-11-15)

Pricing mapping guidelines (draft):
- List price should be conservative vs direct sales to avoid arbitrage. Include marketplace fees (e.g., 20% platform fee) when computing effective price.
- Use per-GPU-equivalent or per-inference-unit abstraction in marketplace metadata to help buyers compare cost.
- For private/on-prem, present as "Platform license + optional deployment services" with SOW engagement for install.

2) Copy variants and metadata fields (short + long examples)
- Elevator (1 line): "Redwood Inference — predictable, low-latency LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- Short (25–40 words): "Run LLM inference reliably at scale. Redwood delivers predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise-ready private deployments with SLA-backed dedicated capacity and KMS integration."
- Mid (80–120 words): "Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for production LLM serving. Choose hosted API for rapid integration, reserved Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, or Private deployments for regulated data needs. Features include real-time streaming, automatic KV caching, model version pinning, and rollout controls—plus observability dashboards and cost-optimization recommendations. Ideal for engineering teams building mission-critical LLM features."
- Long (300–400 words): draft full product paragraph + bullets for features, security/compliance, and support tiers. (Keep in doc to iterate with product/engineering).

Copy notes / marketplace quirks: list prices often appear on public pages; avoid including a free-trial credit amount in long copy if marketplace shows it inconsistently. Some marketplaces truncate descriptions — ensure critical security claims appear in first 160 characters.

3) Security & compliance preflight (checklist)
- Required artifacts to upload/check (per marketplace):
  - Data handling statement (short): "No customer data retained beyond request scope unless customer enables log storage."
  - PII handling and DPA pointer (link to legal DPA doc): include contact for legal review.
  - KMS integration notes: supported KMS providers, whether keys leave customer control.
  - SOC/ISO attestation: include latest audit dates and scope.
  - VPC connectivity instructions and diagrams for private deployments.
  - Pen-test summary and remediation notes.
- Marketplace-specific items to confirm:
  - AWS Marketplace: AMI/Container listing security scan reports; ensure ECR image has image scanning enabled.
  - Azure Marketplace: CIS baseline checklist + publisher verification doc.
  - GCP Marketplace: deployment manager / helm chart security validation.
- Action items:
  - (Priya) Provide DPA & SOC doc links -> due 2025-11-09.
  - (Noah) Export container SBOM for listing -> due 2025-11-12.

4) Technical assets and QA test plan
- Required uploadables: icon (1024px), hero image, 1-line tagline, 3–5 screenshots (console, dashboard), short demo video (90s), pricing JSON, billing SKU mapping file, terms & contact.
- Test steps:
  - Provision via marketplace test flow in staging account and verify provisioning time < 30 mins for hosted SKU.
  - For Dedicated: validate autoscaling policy applied by marketplace provisioning and run throughput test to confirm baseline.
  - For Private: verify installer script runs in customer VPC and KMS integration completes.
  - Validate telemetry: confirm logs show marketplace purchase transaction IDs and SKU mapping tags for reconciliation with billing.
- QA owners: engineering-ops to run provisioning tests; product to validate copy rendering in each marketplace UI.

5) Ops & billing reconciliation notes
- Ensure marketplace SKU codes map to internal billing product codes; include mapping file in PR to billing. Linked artifact: internal pricebook entry (add link once available).
- Reconciliation frequency: weekly during launch ramp, then monthly.
- Dispute path: finance lead to reconcile vendor payout differences and adjust accounting ledger.

6) Launch timeline (proposed)
- Week 0: finalize legal artifacts and pricing mapping.
- Week 1: prepare asset bundle + copy + images.
- Week 2: engineering provisioning tests in marketplace staging.
- Week 3: submit listings for vendor review.
- Week 4–6: marketplace review cycles and iterate.
- Post-launch: monitoring cadence: daily checks for first 2 weeks, then weekly.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress)
- Should we list Dedicated burst capacity as a separate add-on? (Pricing to decide)
- How to represent free-trial credits on marketplaces that don't permit promotional credits in the listing? (Growth input needed)
- Confirm legal approval for the indemnity paragraph: JIRA MKTP-4123 (blocking).
- Localization: which non-English locales are MUST for launch? (E.g., de, fr for EU targets)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a lightweight, operational runbook — expect many short bullet points and action items. Please add comments inline in the Google Doc or annotate here.
- If you are an engineer: add exact artifact names (e.g., image: ghcr.io/redwood/release/marketplace:v1.2.0) and test accounts used.
- If you are from legal/compliance: paste final DPA and SOC/ISO artifact links here.

Version history (quick):
- 2025-11-02 created by Marina Patel (initial SKU mapping + copy stubs)
- 2025-11-10 Priya Shah added security artifact checklist and AWS-specific notes
- 2026-02-20 Diego Alvarez updated pricing guidance and linked PR to marketplace assets

End of runbook.

-- quick signoff checklist (copyable):
[ ] Pricing mapping approved by pricing lead
[ ] Legal artifacts uploaded (DPA, SOC)
[ ] Engineering provisioning tests green in staging
[ ] Marketplace asset bundle uploaded and submitted
[ ] Billing SKU mapping file committed

(Comments and incremental edits expected)
